class.name: DmabufImage
class.brief_description: A Linux dmabuf imported as a Vulkan image, sampled without copies.
class.description: Imports an NV12 dmabuf (for example a frame from a hardware video decoder) once, as a multi-planar Vulkan image, and makes one [RenderingDevice] texture per plane: Y as [constant RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R8_UNORM] and interleaved CbCr as [constant RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R8G8_UNORM] at half size. Wrap them in [Texture2DRD] to use them in materials. The producer and the GPU take turns with the memory: call [method acquire] after the producer has finished writing a frame and before the planes are sampled, and [method release] before the producer writes to the buffer again. Only available with the Vulkan rendering driver on Linux. Call the methods on the rendering thread.

method.name: acquire
method.description: Takes the image from the producer: records a queue family ownership transfer from the foreign queue family, from the GENERAL layout to the shader read-only layout. Does nothing if the image is already acquired.

method.name: free_image
method.description: Frees the plane textures. The Vulkan image and memory are destroyed once the GPU can no longer use them, the next time any [DmabufImage] is imported, acquired, released or freed; at engine shutdown they are left to the process exit. Free any [Texture2DRD] that wraps the planes first.

method.name: get_drm_modifier
method.description: Returns the DRM format modifier of the imported image.

method.name: get_image_count
method.description: Returns 1 when both planes are views of one Vulkan image. Returns 2 when the dmabuf was imported as two Vulkan images with the same layout, one per plane view (see [method import_nv12]). Returns 0 when nothing is imported.

method.name: get_plane_rid
method.description: Returns the [RenderingDevice] texture of the plane: 0 for Y, 1 for CbCr.

method.name: get_size
method.description: Returns the size of the image (the size of the Y plane).

method.name: get_q10c_candidates
method.description: The ways to import the decoder's [code]Q10C[/code] buffers (UBWC-compressed TP10) that the Vulkan driver says it can import from a dmabuf and sample, best first: one [Dictionary] each with [code]format[/code] (a VkFormat), [code]format_name[/code], [code]modifier[/code] (a DRM format modifier), [code]memory_planes[/code], [code]layout[/code] ([code]meta[/code]: each memory plane starts at its UBWC metadata; [code]data[/code]: at its pixels; [code]4plane[/code]: Y, UV, Y metadata, UV metadata; [code]1plane[/code]), [code]source[/code] and [code]description[/code]. By default every non-linear modifier the driver lists for [code]G10X6_B10X6R10X6_2PLANE_420_UNORM_3PACK16[/code]; the environment variables [code]HWVIDEO_Q10C_FORMAT[/code] (a VkFormat number, or G10X6, G12X4, G16), [code]HWVIDEO_Q10C_MODIFIER[/code] (hexadecimal) and [code]HWVIDEO_Q10C_LAYOUT[/code] override, and [code]HWVIDEO_Q10C=0[/code] turns it off. Looked once per process; empty without a Vulkan [RenderingDevice] that has DRM format modifiers, dmabuf import and [code]samplerYcbcrConversion[/code] ([method get_q10c_report] says why).

method.name: get_q10c_disabled_reason
method.description: Why Q10C through the YCbCr sampler is off for the rest of the run (no candidate imported, or the picture check of [HWVideoTexture] saw noise); empty if it isn't.

method.name: get_q10c_report
method.description: What the driver lists for the Q10C formats, which modifiers it refused, and the candidates (see [method get_q10c_candidates]).

method.name: get_supported_nv12_modifiers
method.description: Returns the DRM format modifiers with which the device can sample NV12 images. Run with [code]--verbose[/code] to also print the memory plane count and features of each.

method.name: import_nv12
method.description: Imports the dmabuf [param fd] as an NV12 image. Give one offset and one row pitch per memory plane of the modifier (2 for [code]DRM_FORMAT_MOD_LINEAR[/code]). The fd is duplicated, so the caller still owns it. For Qualcomm UBWC ([code]DRM_FORMAT_MOD_QCOM_COMPRESSED[/code], 0x0500000000000001, a decoder's Q08C buffers) give 2 memory planes: the offset of each is where its compression metadata starts, and the pitch is the pitch of its pixels. Turnip keeps UBWC on a mutable NV12 image only if all its view formats compress alike, which R8 and R8G8 don't. When the driver refuses the image with both view formats, the dmabuf is imported twice instead, as two images with the same layout: one with only the R8 view of plane 0, one with only the R8G8 view of plane 1. [method get_image_count] tells which.

method.name: import_p010
method.description: Imports the dmabuf [param fd] as a P010 image ([code]VK_FORMAT_G10X6_B10X6R10X6_2PLANE_420_UNORM_3PACK16[/code]: 16-bit samples, the 10 bits in the high bits), the same way as [method import_nv12]. The plane views are R16 (Y, in [code]r[/code]) and R16G16 at half size (Cb in [code]r[/code], Cr in [code]g[/code]). Give the offsets and pitches from the decoder's plane info: the pitch is its [code]bytesperline[/code] (at least twice the width).

method.name: get_ycbcr_description
method.description: For a YCbCr import: its format, modifier and chroma siting.

method.name: import_ycbcr
method.description: Imports a 2-plane 4:2:0 dmabuf as one multi-planar image of [param vk_format] with the explicit DRM format modifier and memory planes (one offset and pitch each), read only through a sampler with a YCbCr conversion (RGB_IDENTITY, full range: the raw codes). [method acquire] records a compute pass into the [RenderingDevice] graph that writes the frame into [param out_y] (R16_UNORM, full size) and [param out_cbcr] (R16G16_UNORM, half size), both [RenderingDevice] textures with storage use, as P010 holds it (each code in the high bits), so shaders read it like a P010 frame; [method release] does nothing (the pass hands the dmabuf back). [method get_plane_rid] returns the out textures, which stay the caller's. For [code]Q10C[/code], whose samples (TP10) have no plane view format: the driver decompresses and unpacks it in the sampler, if it supports it.

method.name: import_ycbcr_test_pattern
method.description: The YCbCr pass of [method import_ycbcr] on a linear host-memory test pattern ([code]G10X6_B10X6R10X6_2PLANE_420_UNORM_3PACK16[/code], or [code]G8_B8R8_2PLANE_420_UNORM[/code] with [param bits] 8), for drivers without dmabufs: after [method acquire], [param out_y] and [param out_cbcr] hold the P010 form of the pattern exactly.

method.name: import_planes
method.description: Imports each plane of the dmabuf [param fd] (1 or 2) as its own single-plane image of [param format] ([constant RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM], [constant RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_A2B10G10R10_UNORM_PACK32], [constant RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R16G16_UNORM] or [constant RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R32_UINT]), with the given size in texels, offset and row pitch; the modifier must have one memory plane for that format. Plane [code]i[/code] is then the whole of image [code]i[/code]. With [param mutable], the images are mutable to a format of another UBWC class (R32_UINT, or R8G8B8A8 for R32_UINT); the driver's format query is reported but not enforced then. Experimental: used for 10-bit [code]Q10C[/code] decoder buffers (see [member HWVideoTexture.q10c_view]).

method.name: import_test_pattern
method.description: Creates a linear NV12 dmabuf filled with a test pattern and imports it with [method import_nv12]. The buffer is a DRM dumb buffer on [param device], or comes from [code]/dev/udmabuf[/code] if that fails. With [param device] set to [code]"host"[/code], no dmabuf is used: the pattern goes into a linear image in host-visible Vulkan memory, which tests the plane views, ownership transfers and shader on any Vulkan driver (e.g. lavapipe). [code]"host-split"[/code] does the same with two images bound to the same memory, one per plane view, as a split import makes them. [code]"host-p010"[/code] and [code]"host-p010-split"[/code] do the same in P010 (as [method import_p010]), with each 8-bit value [code]v[/code] stored as [code]v << 8[/code], so a P010 shader shows the same picture. Luma rises from left to right with a white grid every eighth of the size; Cb rises from top to bottom and Cr from left to right.

method.name: is_acquired
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] between [method acquire] and [method release].

method.name: is_imported
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if an image is imported.

method.name: release
method.description: Gives the image back to the producer: records a queue family ownership transfer to the foreign queue family, from the shader read-only layout to the GENERAL layout. The producer must not write to the buffer until the GPU has finished the frame in which this was recorded. Does nothing if the image is not acquired.

method.name: is_q10c_available
method.description: Whether 10-bit video can go to [code]Q10C[/code] through the YCbCr import: there is a candidate and it hasn't failed in this run.

method.name: is_ycbcr
method.description: Whether the image is a YCbCr import ([method import_ycbcr]).
